Phase 3 · Assessment reference

Assessment & Submission

The final committee decision is evaluated as both an auditable technical package and a persuasive oral defense.

Canvas is the submission authority

Canvas remains the authority for due dates, submission mechanics, and the project's course-grade weight. The criteria below preserve the written/oral balance while assessing both individual role ownership and the committee's integrated decision.

Written package · 50% of Phase 3 assessment

Technical evidence

CriterionWeightCommittee-ready standard
Evidence quality & technical accuracy25%Claims, calculations, formulas, sources, FactSet retrieval records, as-of dates, and portfolio metrics are correct, comparable, traceable, and interpreted; required licensed evidence is submitted privately through Canvas and AI output is never treated as evidence.
Security analysis & selection20%Bond, mutual-fund, and ETF choices follow real candidate comparisons and address return drivers, risks, costs, duration/credit or benchmark/style exposure, liquidity, diversification, Issuer Reality Checks, and monitoring.
Client suitability & IPS compliance20%Each recommendation traces to Phase 1 client needs and guardrails, and the IPS scorecard tests all relevant objectives and RRTTLLU constraints.
Portfolio integration & risk response20%Weights, diversification, overlap, risk exposures, bear-case results, breaches, corrective trades, and re-tests form one internally consistent portfolio decision.
Role ownership & team decision trail15%Each analyst's owned work is identifiable, peer-reviewed, and integrated into votes, dissent, action items, visual exhibits, and the Analyst Decision Log.

Oral defense · 50% of Phase 3 assessment

Investment-committee pitch

CriterionWeightCommittee-ready standard
Live defense & evidence response25%Members answer the question asked, use relevant evidence and calculations, acknowledge uncertainty, and defend or revise the judgment under challenge.
Individual role ownership25%Each member demonstrates command of the work they owned and can explain the decision, evidence, AI challenge, verification, and limitations.
Team integration20%The committee presents one coherent chain from client discovery through security selection, allocation, stress results, correction, and final recommendation.
Client suitability & risk compliance20%Members can show where client needs changed the portfolio, explain the strongest bear case, and defend compliance or the corrective action taken.
Clarity, professionalism & visual evidence10%The team communicates concisely as client-focused professionals and uses legible exhibits that make the recommendation, trade-offs, and evidence visible.

Live defense question bank

Prepare to defend owned work and the integrated decision

The panel may direct any question to any member. Role ownership determines preparation responsibility, not permission to ignore the rest of the portfolio.

Client and Macro Strategist

  • Which Phase 1 client fact or guardrail most changed the final portfolio, and where can the committee see that change?
  • Which macro assumption matters most to this recommendation, and what evidence would cause the team to revise it?
  • Which unresolved client information gap remains material, and how did the portfolio avoid pretending it was known?

Fixed-Income Analyst

  • Why does the selected fixed-income exposure fit the client's cash-flow horizon better than the strongest alternative?
  • What happens to price and income if rates or credit spreads move against the position, and which duration or credit evidence supports that answer?
  • What did the Issuer Reality Check reveal about cash flow, leverage, interest coverage, maturities, and the largest issuer-specific risk?

Fund and ETF Analyst

  • Why is this mutual fund or ETF the best implementation vehicle after fees, trading costs, taxes, liquidity, and benchmark/style exposure?
  • What did the look-through Issuer Reality Check reveal about the most material relevant holding, overlap, concentration, and actual diversification?
  • Which performance or tracking comparison is decision-useful, and how did you make the periods and as-of dates comparable?

Portfolio Manager and Risk Analyst

  • Which risk contributes most to the portfolio's bear-case loss, and which client goal is therefore most exposed?
  • Show the IPS compliance test. Which metric came closest to a warning or breach, and what action follows?
  • If the committee rejects one proposed adjustment, what alternative preserves the client goal and what new trade-off does it create?

Any committee member

  • What was the team's strongest initial judgment that changed after AI challenge and human verification?
  • Which FactSet retrieval most affected the recommendation, how did you interpret it, and where is the licensed-source evidence retained under course policy?
  • Which source or calculation carries the most decision weight, and what are its limitations?
  • What is the strongest reasonable case against the final recommendation?
  • What monitoring trigger would force the committee to reconvene before the normal review date?

Final readiness check

Before the committee meeting

  • Executive recommendation and decision memo
  • Technical exhibit book linking macro, mandate, allocation, securities, and risk
  • Client-specific recommendation for all three assigned clients
  • Final decision record with vote, reservations, and implementation actions
  • Visual oral presentation with balanced speaking time
  • Cross-functional Q&A preparation

Q&A standard

Every member must be able to defend the market view, mandate, allocation, security choices, stress test, and trade-offs. The panel may direct a question to a member who did not lead that workstream.
